name: lentil wellington
instructions:
From Nisha Vora (Rainbow Plant Life). A vegan wellington built on a lentil-and-mushroom log filling wrapped in puff pastry — no vegan filets, no seared protein slabs. The whole roast is one continuous savory-baked log, umami-forward from mushrooms + walnuts + miso + nutritional yeast + tomato paste. Called 'lentil wellington' because the lentils are what actually holds the log together — the meat-analog-in-pastry format depends on cooked lentils as the bind.

Serves 8. Total time ~2.5 hours (20 min prep, 2 hr 10 min cook + bake).

=== FILLING INGREDIENTS ===
- ~1/3 cup (60g) dried brown or green lentils (~6 oz cooked) — or use pre-cooked lentils as a shortcut
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small yellow onion, chopped
- 6 garlic cloves, chopped
- 8 oz (~227g) mushrooms — Nisha uses a mix of shiitake and cremini; any mushroom works (see notes)
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried)
- 1 tbsp fresh rosemary leaves, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
- 1 tsp sweet or hot paprika (optional — adds reddish color)
- freshly cracked black pepper
- 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- 1 cup (~110g) walnuts, toasted (see notes — don't skip toasting)
- 2 tbsp white or yellow (light) miso paste
- 2 tbsp nutritional yeast
- 1 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1/4 cup (~20g) panko breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup (32g) all-purpose flour

=== PASTRY ===
- 1 sheet vegan puff pastry (Pepperidge Farms is naturally vegan; check label)
- flour for rolling
- 1 tbsp unsweetened plant-based milk
- 1 tbsp olive oil or neutral oil
- coarse/flaky sea salt for topping

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. COOK THE LENTILS: instant pot — 2/3 cup water + pinch salt, pressure cook high 6 min, natural release 10 min (repeat 1-2 min if not tender). Stovetop — cover lentils with water, boil then simmer covered 20-30 min until tender-not-mushy. Drain any excess. Transfer to a bowl and REFRIGERATE until fully cooled.

2. FINELY CHOP THE MUSHROOMS: pulse in a food processor several times until finely chopped, or knife-chop fine.

3. COOK THE MUSHROOM MIXTURE: heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high. Add onions + small pinch of salt; cook 7-10 min stirring occasionally until softened and golden brown. Add garlic, mushrooms, thyme, rosemary, paprika, black pepper; cook ~5 min until mushrooms are softened and their liquid has evaporated. Add 1 tsp salt and cook 1 more min. Transfer to fridge to cool completely.

4. TOAST + GRIND THE WALNUTS: skillet on medium-low 3-5 min tossing frequently, OR oven at 350°F 8-10 min. Cool slightly. Pulse in food processor to fine crumbs — DON'T over-process into walnut butter.

5. PREHEAT OVEN TO 375°F (190°C).

6. MAKE THE FILLING: add cooled lentils + cooled mushroom mixture to the food processor, plus miso, nutritional yeast, tomato paste, and lemon juice. Blend until somewhat smooth, slightly sticky, and coming together. Add the ground walnuts, panko, AND THE 1/4 CUP ALL-PURPOSE FLOUR (don't forget the flour — commonly overlooked; see notes); blend again until well incorporated. If the filling is warm, refrigerate 15-30 min to make it moldable.

7. FORM + BAKE THE LOG: line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment. Turn out the filling and hand-form into a log — roughly 7 in long x 4.5-5 in wide (18 cm x 11.5-12.5 cm), no taller than 1 in. Bake at 375°F for 35 min until firm to the touch and slightly brown/crisp outside (internal temp 200-205°F / 94-96°C). Cool COMPLETELY. Turn oven off.

8. THAW THE PUFF PASTRY: while log cools, lay puff pastry on a lightly floured surface. Thaw at room temp 20-30 min (no longer — see notes on keeping cold).

9. ROLL + BRAID: roll pastry to ~9 x 13 inches. Place cooled log in the middle so the log's top and bottom nearly touch the pastry edges widthwise. With a paring knife, cut 1-inch strips on each side about 1/4 of the way in (not quite reaching the log) — ~9 strips per side. Whisk plant milk + oil = vegan egg wash. Brush each strip with egg wash. Braid alternating strips over the top of the log. Pinch and tuck the top/bottom edges closed; brush with more egg wash to seal.

10. VENT + REST: lightly prick the top of the pastry all over with a fork (steam venting). Transfer wellington to a fresh parchment-lined sheet pan. Brush the rest of the egg wash all over; sprinkle flaky sea salt on top. Refrigerate 15-20 min to re-chill the pastry (critical — see two-temperature note).

11. TWO-TEMPERATURE BAKE: preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Bake 25 min. Increase to 425°F (218°C) and bake 10 more min until golden brown, flaky, puffed, and internal temp reads 200-205°F. See notes on why the two-temp system matters.

12. REST + SLICE: cool 10 min before slicing. Serve plain or with mushroom gravy (see gravy component below).

=== OPTIONAL — MUSHROOM GRAVY (SEPARATE, SERVE ALONGSIDE) ===

Nisha frames the gravy as optional ('the loaf is rich and moist enough to do without'). Same ingredient overlap with the filling — batch-prep alongside.

INGREDIENTS:
- 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 small yellow onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried)
- 1 tbsp fresh rosemary leaves, chopped
- 2 cups (~150-200g) chopped cremini (or other brown-button) mushrooms
- black pepper to taste
- 1/2 tsp kosher salt
- 3 tbsp arrowroot powder or cornstarch
- 1 1/2 cups (360 mL) low-sodium vegetable stock
- 1 tbsp white or yellow (light) miso paste

PROCEDURE:
1. Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high. Add onions and cook ~4 min until softening. Add garlic, mushrooms, thyme, rosemary, black pepper; cook until mushrooms reduce and liquid mostly (not fully) evaporates. Add 1/2 tsp salt; cook 1 more min.
2. Add arrowroot/cornstarch, whisk to coat, cook 1 min. Pour in vegetable stock; bring to a simmer, whisk 2 min until thickened.
3. Transfer to a blender, add miso, blend smooth. Return to pan, low heat 3-5 min to thicken further. Adjust seasoning.

Gravy keeps 4-5 days in the fridge, 1 month in freezer.
notes:
Nisha Vora's Lentil Wellington (Rainbow Plant Life), by the book. See the FAILED SPIN-OFF ATTEMPT section below for a documented WIP experiment (tomato-free vegetarian mince meat) that used this recipe as a base and eventually plateaued. For a related british-cottage-pie approach on a completely different scaffold (Jamie Oliver's), see [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]].

=== TOASTED WALNUTS ARE THE ONLY VALID NUT — ALMONDS OR RAW WALNUTS ACTIVELY MAKE THE DISH WORSE ===

This is the load-bearing rule for the whole umami stack. The filling reads unmistakably meaty despite being fully plant-based, and TOASTED WALNUTS are where that meatiness actually comes from — not the mushrooms, not the miso, not the tomato paste. Toasting generates a background campfire savoriness that ties the loaf together and pushes the filling into meat-analog territory; the mushroom + miso + nutritional yeast + tomato paste stack extends that base but can't create it.

This is not a 'walnut or another nut' slot and not a 'walnut, toasted or raw' slot — it's specifically toasted walnuts, and the substitutions people reach for actively make the dish worse:

- ALMONDS MAKE IT WORSE. Too sweet-mild, wrong texture — no meaty chewy body. Almonds in the filling read as sweet-crunchy against the savory-earthy stack, and the loaf loses its meat-analog register. Marked clashing.
- RAW/UNTOASTED WALNUTS MAKE IT WORSE. Raw walnut reads flat and slightly astringent — it takes the umami slot without filling it, muting the surrounding aromatics without contributing anything of its own. You end up with less flavor than you'd get from a walnut-free version.

Toast: 3-5 min in a skillet on medium-low tossing frequently, OR 8-10 min at 350°F in the oven. Watch closely; walnuts burn fast once they hit the sweet spot.

Don't OVER-process the toasted walnuts either. Pulse just to fine crumbs — beyond that they release oil and turn into walnut butter, which changes the filling texture from meaty-chunky to greasy-smooth.

=== COMMONLY FORGOTTEN — THE FLOUR IN THE FILLING (STEP 6) ===

The 1/4 cup (32g) all-purpose flour that goes INTO THE FILLING alongside the panko in step 6 is easy to overlook — it's listed among the filling ingredients rather than in a distinct thickening step, and it gets pulsed in with the walnuts and panko as the last-stage absorber.

What happens if you forget: filling is wetter and stickier than it should be, doesn't hold its log shape, and the interior stays under-set even after the 35-min bake. Panko alone doesn't absorb enough moisture. Check the flour is in before you close the food processor.

=== COOL EVERYTHING BEFORE BLENDING ===

Both the lentils AND the sautéed mushroom mixture need to be fully cool before they meet the food processor. Warm ingredients turn the filling too sticky to shape — you'll get a wet paste that won't hold a log. Fridge time is real cook time here; plan for it. If you're in a hurry, spread the cooked components on a sheet pan (thin layer = fast cooling) instead of leaving them in a bowl.

=== KEEP THE PASTRY COLD ===

Puff pastry works because of thin butter/fat layers between dough layers — those layers steam-puff during baking. If the pastry warms up too much (over 30 min at room temp, or from being worked with warm hands), the fat softens and integrates into the dough, and the pastry won't puff — it'll just bake flat.

- Thaw the pastry no more than 30 min at room temp (Nisha's cap). If you need longer, thaw in the fridge.
- After assembly (which puts warm hands on the pastry), rest the assembled wellington in the fridge 15-20 min BEFORE it goes into the oven. This isn't optional — Nisha specifically notes that skipping this step causes uneven baking.
- Don't have a rolling pin? Nisha suggests a chilled wine bottle. Same principle: cold surface, minimal warming.

=== THE TWO-TEMPERATURE BAKE — LOAD-BEARING ===

375°F for 25 min, then 425°F for 10 min. Not one temperature the whole way.

Nisha tested both single-temp approaches and both failed:
- ALL AT 425°F: top browns too fast; inner dough doesn't fully bake through.
- ALL AT 375°F: dough bakes through but pastry isn't beautifully golden.
- SOLUTION: start at 375°F to let the inner dough cook through gently, then finish at 425°F to blast the exterior into golden-puffed territory.

Don't hedge to 400°F the whole time. The two-temperature system is what gives you both structural doneness AND the finished exterior color.

=== FLAKY SALT ON TOP IS NOT OPTIONAL ===

Coarse or flaky sea salt sprinkled on the pastry before baking is one of those low-effort finishes that changes the whole eating experience. The salt crystals crunch against the flaky pastry and contrast with the softer savory filling underneath. Regular table salt doesn't do this — the crystal structure has to be big enough to survive the bake. Maldon or similar flaky sea salt is what you want.

=== MUSHROOM CHOICE — MIX IS BETTER THAN ONE VARIETY ===

Nisha uses a mix of shiitake and cremini. Any mushroom works but a mix reads more interesting than one variety alone — different mushroom species have different flavor profiles and moisture contents.

- SHIITAKE: earthier, more umami-forward, denser.
- CREMINI (brown button): milder, sweeter, more familiar 'mushroom' flavor.
- WHITE BUTTON: higher water content — cook longer to drive off moisture, or the filling stays wet.
- PORTABELLA: works, deeper meatier flavor; tilts the loaf more assertively mushroomy.

All valid. The shiitake + cremini mix Nisha uses is the solid default.

=== MISO + NUTRITIONAL YEAST HERE IS A LEGITIMATE WIN ===

Miso + nutritional yeast is the classic 'vegan glutamate bomb' — a shortcut I'm generally critical of. It works here because it sits inside a broader flavor architecture: toasted walnuts (roasty), mushrooms (glutamate + texture), tomato paste (concentrated sweet-savory), thyme + rosemary (herbal woodsy), lemon juice (bright), sautéed onion + 6 garlic cloves (structural aromatics). The miso + nooch add depth to that stack rather than substituting for it. See [[feedback_vegan_glutamate]] for the general principle: bad as the WHOLE umami stack; good as part of a broader one.

=== MAKE-AHEAD OPTIONS ===

Nisha provides two make-ahead paths:
1. FILLING AHEAD: make the mushroom-lentil log through step 7 (bake and cool), refrigerate up to 2 days. On serving day, wrap in pastry and bake per steps 8-12. Better option for planning — the pastry-wrap-and-bake step is the shortest part.
2. FULLY-ASSEMBLED-UNBAKED AHEAD: assemble the wellington through step 10, wrap tightly and refrigerate up to 1 day. Bake as directed on serving day.

=== GRAVY IS OPTIONAL (NISHA'S OWN NOTE) ===

Nisha explicitly says 'personally, I think this loaf is rich and moist enough to do without the gravy.' The filling has enough umami and moisture on its own. Make the gravy if serving to guests who expect wellington-with-gravy or for a fancier presentation; skip it for a simpler execution. Ingredient overlap with the filling means batch-prep is efficient if you want it.

=== VARIATIONS FROM THE COMMENTS SECTION (WORTH KNOWING) ===

- COMMENTER 'ANN': subbed eggplant for mushrooms, doubled seasonings. Reported success. Interesting variation to try if mushrooms aren't around.
- COMMENTER 'DAKSHA': accidentally over-processed mushrooms to a very fine ground-beef-like texture; reported it turned out well anyway. Suggests the mushroom-chop coarseness has some flexibility.

=== FAILED SPIN-OFF ATTEMPT — TOMATO-FREE VEGETARIAN MINCE MEAT (WIP) ===

Documenting an unsuccessful experimental spin-off from this recipe. Goal: use Nisha's lentil + mushroom + nut umami base to build a TOMATO-FREE vegetarian MINCE MEAT — a filling that reads meaty and dense enough to serve inside pies without relying on tomato as a depth ingredient. Kept here as a WIP record because the lessons transferred to other work; the direction itself plateaued.

THE EXPERIMENTAL ARC:

1. Started with Nisha's filling as the base (this recipe).
2. First anglican departure: butter + worcestershire/tamarind + dried dill instead of olive oil + tomato paste + fresh rosemary. Distinctly more british.
3. Discovered HAMBURGER-Y HAZARD — FRESH DILL + TOMATO PASTE + FRESH DICED ONIONS together push the loaf into a diner meatloaf register. If going anglican with dill, you have to drop the tomato paste AND swap to onion powder — the three fresh/tomato ingredients belong together or all out; mixing them leaves you in hamburger territory.
4. Added crushed garlic LATE for bite (rather than sautéed with the mushrooms) — keeps some raw-garlic sharpness in the finished loaf.
5. Tried PUREED CELERY with the mushrooms for depth — REJECTED. Pushed the filling into stew territory quickly. (Celery ROOT / celeriac is different — see [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]] which uses it cleanly.)
6. HEAVY CREAM discovered as the biggest upgrade. 3-4 tbsp stirred into the filling after processing keeps it from drying out during the bake. Pureed lentils sponge the cream so it doesn't read creamy — just adds fat and satisfaction.
7. Tried FRENCH DIRECTION (dijon mustard + tarragon instead of worcestershire + dill) — REJECTED. Fine but didn't add much over dill + thyme.
8. LEMON JUICE is a required brightener — leaving it out leaves the filling noticeably flat.
9. Restructured as a pot pie (skipping wellington's log-and-braid production) to reduce friction.

RESULT: reached 'has potential' but didn't advance to 'excellent.' The line plateaued. Eventually reset to a different scaffold entirely (Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie — see [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]] for that direction).

WHAT THE EXPERIMENT TAUGHT (LESSONS THAT TRANSFERRED):

- The FRESH DILL + TOMATO PASTE + FRESH ONION hazard is a real 3-way combination — worth remembering across any british-vegetarian meat-analog work.
- HEAVY CREAM AS A FILLING HYDRATOR is a load-bearing move that transferred to [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]] as an experimental direction.
- TOASTED WALNUTS stay non-negotiable regardless of direction (see TOASTED WALNUTS ARE THE ONLY VALID NUT above).
- Celery pushes toward stew territory; celery ROOT is different.

IF REVISITING: the fundamental open question is whether Nisha's mushroom + walnut + miso paste can hold a proper meat-pie register WITHOUT tomato paste. Might work with the right depth substitutes — brandy or fortified wine deglaze, dark bouillon, worcestershire + tamarind stack, sherry. Untested combinations worth trying if the mince-meat goal is revived.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[milk-stout-cottage-lentils]]: a different lentil-mushroom pie in the british cottage-pie tradition (Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie as the scaffold — root veg + porcini + marmite + cumin seeds under a mashed potato top). Distinct lineage from this recipe's meat-analog-in-pastry approach; the tomato-free mince-meat spin-off above plateaued and the cottage-pie work moved to Jamie's baseline instead.
- [[french-potato-lentils]]: same lentil + mushroom umami DNA, but in stew form (potato + pureed mushroom + lentil, french). If you like the flavor of this loaf but don't want to bother with pastry, that's the shortcut.
- coq-au-vin, chicken-pot-pie, french-chicken-soup: the french poultry mains this would sit alongside on a holiday table.
